scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Lipschitz Equivalent Separable Banach Spaces Need Not Be Linearly Isomorphic” (preprints/Lipschitz-Equivalent-Separable-Banach-Spaces-Need-Not-Be-Linearly-Isomorphic-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 324 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cc670229303a1ed9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are separable real Banach spaces X, Y and a bijection Ψ : X → Y such that, for every s, t ∈ X, 4 21 ∥s − t∥X ≤ ∥Ψ(s) − Ψ(t)∥Y ≤ 76 25 ∥s − t∥X. (1.1) The space X contains a linearly isometric copy of c0(ℓ2), while Y contains no closed subspace linearly isomorphic to c0(ℓ2). In particular, X and Y are not linearly isomorphic.
